Pilot hole makes your drill go straight. Bigger hole reduces pressures and likelyhood of splitting. Best time to use your anchor is when you park the boat.

1: When you have the proper screw for the substrate you're screwing into. Only soft materials accept pointed screws. For steel and harder substrates, you need a self-tapping screw.

2: Use pilot holes for larger shank diameter screws. Also for precise placement of a screw.

3: An anchor keeps the ship from drifting in heavy winds, fast currents. Lol. ( You have to be more specific as to what type of anchor and what you're anchoring to.)

If your material is soft you can drive the screw directlyinto the material. Eg. screwing 2 pieces of pine together. If your material is substantially harder (Oak, Maple etc) drill a pilot hole to keep the screw from splitting the wood.

Anchors are used to secure fasteners to all kinds of material. You need the right anchor for the right material. Concrete anchors are useless on drywall, and toggles are useless on concrete.
